overview: The Medford School Committee serves as the governing body for Medford Public Schools, responsible for district policy, annual operating budgets, administrative appointment, labor negotiations, and capital infrastructure planning. Across the recorded period spanning May 2019 through October 2026, the committee addressed significant challenges including COVID-19 emergency operations, building safety reviews, elementary overcrowding, and district literacy curriculum alignment. Major long-term initiatives included securing state building grants for a comprehensive high school project, executing multi-million dollar HVAC facility replacements, expanding after-school programming, and managing executive leadership transitions. As of October 2026, the committee selected a geothermal HVAC model for Missituk Elementary, approved construction management models for Roberts Elementary, and reviewed quarterly budget performance alongside expanding after-school operations.

threads.name: Medford High School Building Project and MSBA Core Program
threads.summary: In 2019, the committee created a Master Vision Plan subcommittee to establish a long-term capital strategy for repairing or replacing Medford High School [M05#6]. The committee authorized initial Statements of Interest to the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) Core Program in 2022 and 2023 [M54#3, M81#6]. After invitation into the MSBA eligibility phase [M100#5], the board formally established the Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee in 2024 to oversee governance, educational visioning, and community outreach [M104#5, M105#2]. By 2026, the committee hired Left Field as Owner's Project Manager [M149#5], approved a high school educational plan [M166#3], selected the Construction Manager at Risk delivery method [M168#2], and narrowed project site alternatives down to preferred schematic designs [M176#3, M179#2].

threads.name: School Facilities Maintenance and HVAC Infrastructure
threads.summary: The committee managed persistent facility maintenance challenges across aging district buildings, initially spending free cash on restroom renovations and intercom repairs [M10#4, M10#8]. Following reports of leaking roofs, electrical concerns, and failed cooling infrastructure [M40#6, M92#6], the board authorized technical building assessments and restricted fossil-fuel replacement equipment purchases [M112#6, M112#13]. In 2024 and 2025, the committee authorized major municipal bond issues to fund comprehensive HVAC replacements at McGlynn and Andrews middle schools [M133#6, M146#7]. Infrastructure work extended to elementary facilities in 2026, culminating in approved schematic designs for Roberts Elementary [M187#4] and a geothermal HVAC system selection for Missituk Elementary [M191#4].

threads.name: Elementary School Overcrowding and Space Planning
threads.summary: Surging enrollment created space constraints across elementary facilities, beginning with McGlynn Elementary reaching student capacity in 2021 [M43#5]. By late 2024, staff and committee members highlighted severe overcrowding at Roberts Elementary, leading to calls for district redistricting [M123#8, M124#6]. In 2025, the committee voted to relocate preschool classrooms from Roberts to Missituk to free up space [M152#6] and formed a space planning task force to evaluate facility utilization [M152#7]. Although the committee evaluated middle school grade restructuring models in 2025 [M161#5, M162#5], the board voted in 2026 to delay any grade 5–8 reconfiguration until at least the 2028–2029 school year [M186#4].

threads.name: Before and After-School Care Programs
threads.summary: The committee continuously sought to address long waitlists, facility space limits, and staffing shortages in school-aged childcare [M08#9, M29#9, M48#6]. To reform program delivery, the board established an on-demand lottery system for incoming kindergartners in 2023 [M79#5] and approved tuition increases to cover staff pay hikes [M81#8]. In 2025, the committee partnered with the Belmont After School Enrichment Collaborative (BASIC) to restructure operations [M150#2] and expanded site coordinator positions to full-time status [M155#3]. By late 2026, program adjustments and staff restructuring yielded a 50 percent increase in enrolled students and reduced waitlists [M191#3].

threads.name: Elementary Literacy Curriculum Adoption
threads.summary: In 2019, the district deployed state-funded literacy and dyslexia screening pilots to identify early reading challenges [M05#11, M07#7]. The committee approved adopting the Enhanced Core Reading Instruction (ECRI) program for grades K–2 in early 2020 to strengthen foundational reading instruction [M13#14]. After evaluating multi-year diagnostic assessment data and aligning practices with the science of reading [M73#6, M78#4], the board formally selected Houghton Mifflin Harcourt's 'Into Reading' as the new district-wide elementary literacy core curriculum in June 2023 [M88#5].

threads.name: Labor Contract Negotiations
threads.summary: The committee regularly negotiated collective bargaining agreements across all district labor units. Following prolonged contract negotiations and a formal impasse declaration with the Medford Teachers Association in 2022 [M58#8, M63#5], the board ratified a four-year contract in late 2022 [M73#5] and a successor three-year agreement in 2025 [M148#3]. The committee also completed bargaining agreements for paraprofessionals [M66#2, M121#2, M155#2], school administrators [M94#1, M151#6], cafeteria workers [M117#2], and school nurses [M157#1].

threads.name: Superintendent Executive Leadership
threads.summary: The committee evaluated Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent annually [M03#8, M35#1, M89#2] and extended her contract for four years in 2021 [M29#6]. Following Dr. Edouard-Vincent's departure in January 2025 [M137#3, M138#5], the board appointed Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi as Interim Superintendent [M136#2, M138#3]. After reviewing Dr. Galusi's performance evaluation and leadership entry findings [M160#5, M165#6], the committee voted in February 2026 to appoint Dr. Galusi as permanent superintendent [M166#4] and subsequently approved a three-year executive contract [M177#6].
